name: area-chart
title: Area Chart
description: A trend over time: a smooth line with a gradient fill, plus LineChart for comparing series without fills.

examples.name: area-chart-demo
examples.title: Area chart in a card
examples.description: One series with a gradient fill; hover, touch or arrow keys show the value pill.

examples.name: area-chart-multiple
examples.title: Two series
examples.description: Overlapping areas with a legend; the readout lists every series at that x.

examples.name: area-chart-line
examples.title: Line chart
examples.description: LineChart with three series and dots on each point.

examples.name: area-chart-minimal
examples.title: Minimal
examples.description: Linear curve, no grid and no y axis, for a compact trend.

examples.name: area-chart-table
examples.title: Table view
examples.description: A switch that shows the chart's data table.

props.name: aria-label | aria-labelledby
props.description: Names the chart. One is required; use aria-labelledby to point at a visible card title.

props.name: data
props.description: One object per x position, in order.

props.name: x
props.description: Key of the x value in each row (a month name, a Date, a number).

props.name: series
props.type: { key: string; label: string; color?: string }[]
props.description: What to plot, in palette order (--strata-chart-1..4). Up to 4; past that, fold the tail into "Other". color overrides the palette with a token.

props.name: format
props.type: { value?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions | fn; axis?: …; x?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions | fn }
props.description: Formats values (readout, table, names), y ticks (default: value in compact notation) and x values (Dates default to "12 Mar").

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the plot plus the x axis, in px. The legend sits above it.

props.name: curve
props.description: smooth is monotone cubic: it never overshoots the data, so a peak is never drawn higher than it was.

props.name: showGrid
props.description: Horizontal hairlines at each y tick.

props.name: showXAxis
props.description: X labels, thinned to what fits (always the first and last).

props.name: showYAxis
props.description: Y tick labels in a gutter at the inline start.

props.name: yDomain
props.description: Fixes the y range. Default: nice round numbers around the data, from 0 for areas; fitted for LineChart.

props.name: showTable
props.description: Shows the data table under the chart instead of keeping it visually hidden.

props.name: xLabel
props.description: Header of the table's first column, e.g. "Month".

props.name: summary
props.description: One sentence describing the data for screen readers. Default: generated from the data.

props.name: glow
props.description: A soft halo in the series colour under each line. Decorative.

props.name: showDots
props.description: Ringed dots on every data point.
Same props as AreaChart. No fill, and the y range is fitted to the data instead of starting at 0.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the chart (one tab stop), to the last point you visited or the first.
Moves to the next / previous x position and shows its readout. Mirrored in right-to-left locales.
Jumps to the first / last x position.
Hides the readout without moving focus (WCAG 1.4.13). The next move shows it again.

notes: The plot's hit layer is a React Aria ListBox (horizontal): one option per x position, named with its x and every series value, e.g. "Mar: Revenue $19,800, Costs $13,100". Focusing an option makes the screen reader read it, so no live region is needed.
The ListBox is named by aria-label or aria-labelledby (one is required) and described by a one-sentence summary (generated from the data, or the summary prop).
Every chart also renders its data as a <table> with a caption, visually hidden unless showTable. No value is only reachable by hovering.
The SVG, axis labels and the floating readout are aria-hidden: they repeat what the options and the table say.
Pointer, pen and touch snap to the nearest x position (full-height bands), so nobody has to land on a 2px line or a thin bar.

Text never wears a series colour: labels, axes, legend and readout use text.default and text.subtle; the series colour is only on marks and swatches. Series colours come from --strata-chart-1..4, solved per brand and scheme to reach 3:1 on surfaces and stay distinguishable under colour-vision deficiency.
A 2px focus ring surrounds the plot and axes while an x position has keyboard focus.
Motion (line draw-in, area fade-up, bar growth, readout glide) sits behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
There are no disabled or invalid states: a chart is read-only.

do: Name the chart with aria-labelledby when a card title already says what it shows.
Use AreaChart for one or two series over time; LineChart when comparing three or four.
Format values with Intl options so the readout, table and names read naturally in every locale.
Pass null for a missing value: the line breaks instead of dropping to zero.
dont: Don't plot more than 4 series; fold the tail into "Other" or use small multiples.
Don't put two y scales on one chart; index both series to a common base or use two charts.
Don't colour text with series colours; the legend and readout already key each series.
Don't rely on the chart alone for a number that matters; state it in a heading or stat.
